concepts.name: Levels of Biodiversity: Genetic, Species, and Ecosystem
key_dimensions: Distinction between genetic diversity, species diversity, and ecosystem diversity with examples
Why genetic diversity is the foundation of all other levels — UPSC trap on hierarchical dependency
Measurement indices: Shannon Index, Simpson Index for species diversity
How loss at one level cascades to other levels (e.g., genetic erosion leading to species extinction)

concepts.name: Ecosystem Services Framework (Provisioning, Regulating, Cultural, Supporting)
key_dimensions: Classification per Millennium Ecosystem Assessment (MEA) 2005 — frequently tested source
Distinction between supporting services (primary production, nutrient cycling) vs. provisioning services — common UPSC overlap trap
Economic valuation of ecosystem services: TEEB (The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity) framework
Difference between ecosystem services and ecosystem goods — definitional precision required

concepts.name: Biodiversity and Food Security: Agricultural Biodiversity
key_dimensions: Role of crop wild relatives (CWRs) in developing climate-resilient varieties
Threat of genetic erosion due to monoculture farming — Green Revolution trade-off
International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA) — its Multilateral System
Distinction between ex-situ conservation for food crops (gene banks like NBPGR) vs. in-situ on-farm conservation

concepts.name: Biodiversity as a Source of Pharmaceuticals and Bioprospecting
key_dimensions: Statistics: ~50% of modern drugs derived from natural compounds — significance for healthcare
Bioprospecting vs. biopiracy — definitional boundary and legal implications under CBD/Nagoya Protocol
Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS): obligations on user countries vs. provider countries
Indian cases: Neem patent controversy, Turmeric patent — UPSC favourite examples

concepts.name: Keystone Species and Trophic Cascades
key_dimensions: Definition of keystone species vs. dominant species vs. umbrella species — UPSC trap on overlapping terms
Trophic cascade mechanism: top-down vs. bottom-up regulation with examples (wolf reintroduction in Yellowstone)
Role of keystone species in maintaining ecosystem structure disproportionate to their biomass
Indian examples: Tiger as keystone species and its cascading effects on forest ecosystems

concepts.name: Biodiversity and Climate Regulation
key_dimensions: Role of forests, wetlands, and oceans as carbon sinks — quantitative significance
Biodiversity-climate nexus: how biodiversity loss accelerates climate change and vice versa (dual feedback loop)
Blue carbon ecosystems (mangroves, seagrasses, salt marshes) — distinction from terrestrial carbon sinks
IPBES-IPCC joint report findings on biodiversity-climate interlinkages — policy relevance

concepts.name: Intrinsic vs. Instrumental Value of Biodiversity
key_dimensions: Philosophical distinction: intrinsic value (right to exist regardless of utility) vs. instrumental value (utility to humans)
Biocentric vs. anthropocentric ethical frameworks in conservation policy
Legal recognition of rights of nature: Ecuador, New Zealand — contrast with India's approach
UPSC trap: how intrinsic value argument underpins the precautionary principle in environmental law

concepts.name: Biodiversity Hotspots: Concept and Criteria
key_dimensions: Norman Myers' criteria: ≥1500 endemic vascular plant species AND ≥70% primary vegetation lost — both conditions mandatory (UPSC trap on 'AND' condition)
India's four biodiversity hotspots: Himalayas, Western Ghats & Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, Sundaland — geographic precision
Hotspot vs. Megadiverse country vs. Endemic bird area — distinctions frequently confused
Criticism of hotspot approach: neglects species-rich but less threatened areas like Amazon

concepts.name: Biodiversity and Water Cycle Regulation
key_dimensions: Role of forest biodiversity in precipitation recycling through evapo-transpiration (biotic pump theory)
Wetland biodiversity functions: water purification, flood regulation, groundwater recharge
Loss of riparian vegetation and its impact on river hydrology — policy link to riverine biodiversity protection
Distinction between regulating service (water purification) and provisioning service (freshwater supply)

concepts.name: Biodiversity and Soil Health: Below-Ground Biodiversity
key_dimensions: Role of soil microbiome, earthworms, and fungi (mycorrhizae) in nutrient cycling and soil formation
Below-ground biodiversity as a supporting ecosystem service — often neglected in conservation discourse
Impact of chemical agriculture on soil biodiversity — link to sustainable agriculture policy
Soil biodiversity and its role in carbon sequestration — emerging research area relevant to climate commitments

concepts.name: Pollination Services and Biodiversity: Economic Valuation
key_dimensions: Proportion of global food crops dependent on animal pollination (~75% of flowering plants)
Colony Collapse Disorder (CCD) in bees — causes, consequences, and policy responses
Economic valuation of pollination services: TEEB estimates (~$235–577 billion annually)
Beyond bees: role of butterflies, birds, bats as pollinators — UPSC trap on exclusive focus on bees

concepts.name: Biodiversity and Natural Disaster Risk Reduction
key_dimensions: Mangroves as natural barriers against cyclones and tsunamis — 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami case study
Coral reefs as coastal protection mechanisms and their economic equivalence to hard infrastructure
Ecosystem-based Disaster Risk Reduction (Eco-DRR) vs. traditional engineering approaches
Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030: integration of biodiversity/ecosystem health

concepts.name: Biodiversity and Human Health: One Health Framework
key_dimensions: Dilution effect hypothesis: high biodiversity reduces zoonotic disease transmission risk
Biodiversity loss and emergence of zoonotic diseases: COVID-19, Ebola, Nipah — deforestation link
One Health framework: interconnection of human, animal, and ecosystem health — WHO, FAO, UNEP joint initiative
UPSC trap: One Health vs. EcoHealth vs. Planetary Health — conceptual distinctions

concepts.name: Option Value, Existence Value, and Bequest Value of Biodiversity
key_dimensions: Total Economic Value (TEV) framework: use values (direct, indirect) vs. non-use values (option, existence, bequest)
Option value: keeping future possibilities open — relevance to undiscovered species and genetic resources
Existence value: willingness to pay for species survival even without personal use
UPSC trap: distinguishing quasi-option value (value of retaining options under uncertainty) from option value

concepts.name: Biodiversity and Cultural/Aesthetic/Spiritual Values
key_dimensions: Sacred groves (Dev vans) as traditional biodiversity conservation mechanisms in India
Biocultural diversity: co-evolution of linguistic, cultural, and biological diversity
Article 8(j) of CBD: protection of traditional knowledge associated with biodiversity
Aesthetic and ecotourism value of biodiversity — economic argument for conservation of charismatic megafauna

concepts.name: Biodiversity Stability Hypothesis: Diversity-Stability Relationship
key_dimensions: Insurance hypothesis: higher species diversity provides functional redundancy and ecosystem resilience
Rivet hypothesis (Paul Ehrlich): each species is like a rivet — cumulative loss leads to system collapse
Resistance vs. resilience in ecosystems — distinction important for evaluating biodiversity's role
UPSC trap: monoculture vs. polyculture productivity debate — short-term yield vs. long-term stability

concepts.name: Biodiversity and Biotechnology: Genetic Resources as Raw Material
key_dimensions: Biodiversity as the repository of genetic information for biotechnology, synthetic biology, and gene editing
Digital Sequence Information (DSI) on genetic resources — emerging issue in CBD post-2020 framework (Kunming-Montreal)
Distinction between genetic resources (physical) and DSI (digital) — ABS obligations and loopholes
India's Biological Diversity Act 2002 and its amendment 2023 — relaxation of access rules and controversy

concepts.name: Biodiversity and Livelihoods of Indigenous and Local Communities
key_dimensions: Dependency of tribal communities on biodiversity for food, medicine, and cultural identity
Forest Rights Act 2006: community forest rights vs. individual land rights — biodiversity governance overlap
Joint Forest Management (JFM) vs. Community-Based Natural Resource Management (CBNRM)
UPSC trap: difference between Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers under FRA 2006

concepts.name: Functional Diversity vs. Taxonomic Diversity
key_dimensions: Functional diversity: variety of functional traits in an ecosystem vs. simple species count (taxonomic diversity)
Why functional diversity may be a better predictor of ecosystem services than species richness
Functional redundancy: multiple species performing same ecological role — insurance against extinction
UPSC trap: high species richness does not guarantee high functional diversity — policy implications for conservation prioritization

concepts.name: Biodiversity and the Economy: Natural Capital Accounting
key_dimensions: Natural capital: biodiversity as an economic asset on national balance sheets
Dasgupta Review (2021): economic case for biodiversity — GDP vs. inclusive wealth framework
System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) by UN — India's progress in natural capital accounting
UPSC trap: distinction between GDP (excludes natural capital depreciation) and Genuine Progress Indicator (GPI)
